originality.rationale: FAIL for the final submitted conjunction. The 2023 stack-sorting paper Corollary 3.9 supplies the exact iterate coordinates. The 2025 same-object paper Ake–Lewis–Louie–Vindas-Meléndez Lemma 4.4 computes EVERY successive Euclidean altitude sqrt(i(i+1)), by the explicit nested hyperplanes; these altitudes equal the lengths of the canonical origin-to-vertex edge vectors, implying the alleged new perpendicularity and edge spectrum. More decisively, the PUBLIC full general theorem “Weighted terminal simplices have a sorted active-set formula for their minimum enclosing sphere” already determines the entire minimum ball and positive contacts for conv{-a 1,b_i e_i}, a>0; letting a down to 0 covers this right axis simplex. Setting b_i^2=i(i+1) makes its mu_p=(p-2)/sum b_i^-2 equal n(m-1)(p-2)/p, with exactly the same tail/triangular threshold and contact formulas. Thus the key touted sharp minimum-sphere discovery is a mathematical corollary, not merely same-looking parameters. The remaining inradius follows by standard facet clearances from already implicit orthogonal edge data, with no materially distinct original structural lemma.
residual_risks: The 2025 exact Euclidean altitudes and general weighted terminal source were missed by the superseded source review; older source originality claims must not be treated as current evidence.

An inradius-only special case might be considered a separately expressible identity, but it is an elementary textbook consequence of the source vectors/altitudes without substantiated new mathematical value.
